prompts.prompt:
Create one beautiful high resolution 3D game environment concept image, landscape 3:2. This is a spatial redesign for a tiny traveling frog's home, NOT a screenshot of an existing game. Use the supplied references as follows:
Reference 1 (tall stone-house illustration) controls architecture, natural rock material, handcrafted wood loft, enclosed warm atmosphere and restrained set dressing.
Reference 2 (single 3D green frog) controls the EXACT frog appearance: small squat pale leaf-green traveler, cream belly, wide head, quiet sleepy dark half-lidded eyes, thin little arms and two hind feet; keep this identity.
Reference 3 (small 2D frog reading) controls the unhurried tiny-animal mood, modest blue bedding and travel-home character.

CAMERA A / MASTER LAYOUT: one coherent spacious stone-cave home seen from just inside the southwest/front left entrance corner, looking northeast into the room. An elevated but natural 3/4 view, camera at 3 frog-heights, moderate perspective about 45mm lens; show floor and upper loft, no fisheye, no exaggerated giant foreground objects. The camera is INSIDE the enclosed room: continuous natural stone walls and a curved intact vaulted ceiling fill the scene, no dollhouse cut face, no forest or grass visible outside the room.

Use the frog's standing height as unit F. House usable footprint roughly 15F east-west x 12F north-south, curved walls, vault apex 8F. Rear/north wooden mezzanine spans the back wall only, loft deck at 3.8F, 4F deep. Leave the central and front floor genuinely generous, at least 45% unobstructed walking space. NO large central tree trunk, NO central spiral staircase. Only two slim wooden posts at the front corners of the loft. A straight wooden staircase hugs the RIGHT/east wall, starts near the southeast/front right corner and ascends toward the northeast/back right corner, with safe simple handrail and small consistent treads, reachable loft landing.

Permanent layout anchors (must be clear and coherent for future other camera angles): SMALL single bed with muted BLUE quilt in the northwest/back LEFT loft; little book shelf and pinned travel postcards above bed; small desk and yellow cushion in northeast/back RIGHT loft beside stair landing; one round wood-frame window above/near the bed on the north/back wall; another round wood-frame window on the east/right wall, above the stair. LEFT/west ground wall has a low wood tea kitchen and one cream ceramic kettle, modest cabinet. Under the rear loft is a recessed pantry with jars and one small wooden cupboard door. In the front-center of the room, well away from the stairs, a LITTLE low rounded rectangular wood tea table on a subdued moss woven rug with TWO little floor cushions. One green frog stands next to this table, fully visible, tiny in the large room, about 7-9% of the total image height, never oversized. Empty stone-floor circulation is visible all around this little seating island.
Keep furniture compatible with the frog, NOT human furniture: table top 0.58F high, 2F long x1.2F wide; little bed 2.4F long, 1.45F wide. Furniture is small relative to house, the room feels inviting and spacious, not a furniture showroom. Door if visible 2.3F tall. No extra seating sets, no huge decorative clutter.

Art direction: premium stylized 3D woodland storybook world, softly sculpted warm grey/ivory continuous natural ROCK walls, subtle irregular planes and hairline cracks, matte mineral surface; not stacked brickwork, not bark walls, not white plaster. Cool grey-blue irregular flagstone flooring with fine uneven joints, softly worn edges. Warm mid-brown wood with broad gentle grain, simple blue linen on the bed, muted sage textiles, restrained little pottery. Late-afternoon sunlight from east round window pools across stones; indirect warm bounce, gentle soft ambient occlusion, cozy but readable shadows, nothing blown out or neon. Rock and wood remain distinguishable. Rounded simple forms that can be faithfully modeled in Blender.
Render a finished spatial concept, visually rich in texture but with plenty of breathing room. No text, no UI, no labels, no watermark, no logo, no anime humans, no other animals in this image.

Edit the supplied interior image as the MASTER spatial design. Keep the exact enclosing stone house, camera, perspective, two round windows, rear mezzanine, right-hand stairway, two support posts, daylight, material palette and overall layout. The room still reads too crowded relative to the frog. Make the following precise proportion changes, anchored to the floor so nothing floats:
1. Reduce the frog uniformly to 65% of its current HEIGHT and width, in the same spot beside the tea table. Its height in the final image must be about 95-105 pixels on a 1024px-tall output (roughly one tenth of the frame), not the current 155px. Preserve frog identity perfectly.
2. Reduce the entire ground-floor tea seating island (table, rug, kettle/cups/flowers on it, both cushions) uniformly to 70% of its current dimensions, in the same front-center zone. Tabletop should remain usable at about the frog's waist. Create a broad ring of open stone floor around it, not just shrink the camera image.
3. On the loft, reduce the bed itself, blue quilt and pillows to 65% of current size. Keep it a very small single frog bed resting on the SAME loft floor, back left. Reduce the desk, desk cushion, books and vase to about 70%. Leave more empty loft deck between bed, desk and stairs. Small objects must remain on surfaces, not floating or unattached. Shrink bedroom picture display to suit the small bed.
4. Reduce kitchen worktop height/depth and cookware by 25%, leaving its back against the left wall. Keep pantry tucked under the rear loft.
5. Keep the architectural volume and room boundaries UNCHANGED: do not zoom camera out, do not reduce the house, do not shrink floor stones, do not add new furnishings to fill empty space. The free room feels around 15 frog-heights across. Loft height should feel around 3.8 frog-heights. Keep the right stairs usable with small consistent treads, no giant steps.
Prioritize the feeling of a tiny animal inhabiting a generous but cozy house. Broad negative space around appropriately tiny furniture is the point. Refined stylized Blender-ready 3D concept, warm matte natural stone with big organic planes rather than rock bricks, worn flagstones, warm wood. No text, labels, watermark or outside landscape. Single landscape 3:2 image.

Render a NEW CAMERA VIEW of the EXACT SAME tiny frog's spacious stone home in the supplied image, not a new design. Preserve room proportions, single mezzanine, all wall locations and architectural anchors, exact number of furnishings, their positions, materials, sunlight direction and frog identity. Use the reference as the master visual set. Landscape 3:2, high quality stylized 3D environment concept.
Room geography: front=south, back=north, left=west, right=east. Footprint about 15 frog-heights wide x12 deep; natural stone vaulted ceiling 8 high. Rear/north mezzanine only is 4 deep, deck height3.8; supported by two thin wood posts at front corners. One SMALL BLUE single bed at northwest/back-left of loft. One SMALL wood desk and yellow floor cushion at northeast/back-right loft. One circular north wall window above loft. One circular east wall window above stairs. Straight wooden stairs hug EAST/right wall, climbing from southeast/front to northeast/back. WEST/left ground wall has a small low wooden tea kitchen with cream kettle. Under the rear loft is recessed pantry with open shelves on west side and small brown cupboard door on east side. Ground-floor tea island is front of center with one SMALL rounded rectangular wood table (2F long x1.2F), ONE woven sage rug, ONE mustard cushion and ONE blue cushion. Tiny green frog is beside tea island. Main entrance is in the SOUTH/front wall toward its WEST side, a small round-topped wooden door, CLOSED in this view. A modest wooden coat hook and boot mat near entry, no other doors beyond pantry cupboard.
Critical: frog and furniture stay as SMALL relative to room as this reference. No giant foreground tea table or bed, no multiplying furniture, no huge central tree trunk, no spiral stair. Keep floor circulation broad and empty. Maintain grey-ivory monolithic natural rock with sparse cracks, blue-grey irregular stone flooring, warm worn wood, blue quilt, sage textiles. No external garden visible, camera always inside complete stone walls and ceiling. Round windows may show only softly glowing frosted daylight, not a large outside panorama. No text, UI, annotation, branding or watermarks.
CAMERA B: move camera to the SOUTHEAST/front RIGHT side of the room near the foot of the stairs, looking diagonally NORTHWEST toward the small west-wall kitchen and the north loft. Set eye height approximately 1.8F, use natural 42mm moderate perspective, avoid ultrawide. Compose a distinctly different angle from the supplied frontal-left view. Right stair handrail appears at far right edge receding to upstairs landing, doesn't obstruct the view; blue bed visible high left/back, west tea kitchen now clearly seen in depth on the left, tiny tea island sits mid-ground. We should read enclosure, spacious floor and generous room height from a small inhabitant's viewpoint. Frog remains a modest scale cue about 8-10% image height, whole body visible. The new image is a different camera position, not a crop or horizontal mirror of the reference.

CAMERA C: stand at the CENTER of the NORTH/rear loft edge, camera height about 5.2F above ground (1.4F above loft), looking diagonally downward SOUTHWEST toward the entrance side of this same room. This is the REVERSE view looking AWAY from the original back wall. The north wall bed and desk are largely behind the camera, do NOT place another bed, loft or kitchen on the south wall. A small strip of the current loft floor and its low wood railing can frame the very bottom foreground; do not let it occlude the ground-floor tea group. Below, see the same tea table, rug, two cushions and small frog from above, ringed by generous open flagstone floor. WEST-wall tea kitchen should sit on the image's RIGHT side from this reverse camera; EAST-wall staircase and circular window are toward the image's LEFT side. Across the room the intact SOUTH stone wall and small closed rounded wooden entrance door are visible, completing the enclosure; include rock ceiling curve along top of image. Natural restrained 45mm perspective, not an open-roof dollhouse, no exterior view, no added second floor opposite. The reverse view must demonstrate empty circulation and believable scale, not turn into another frontal picture of the back loft.

Create a polished 3D CHARACTER CONCEPT TURNAROUND for a cozy woodland traveling-animal game. Landscape 3:2 studio sheet. The supplied 3D frog is the visual style anchor only: match its simple rounded sculpted forms, restrained sleepy expression, matte smooth surface, cream belly, short limbs and understated Japanese storybook traveler mood. Do not put a frog head on the new animal. The supplied illustrated animal gathering is mood reference for charming little woodland visitors, not a composition to copy.

One species, the SAME single character in three equal-sized full-body views across the image: front at left, clean left-facing side profile in middle, back view at right. All three stand on the same floor baseline, same scale and exact same proportions and markings; show feet and ears fully with clean separation. Background solid warm ivory with soft ground contact shadows, no environment, no text, no labels or watermarks.
Production-friendly anatomy: recognizable species, rounded chunky body, large simple head, tiny restrained face; two distinct short weight-bearing legs with visible feet, two separate little arms slightly away from torso, suitable for later walking and hopping rig; no fused legs, no human clothing, no human hands, no giant glass eyes, no glossy vinyl, no realistic strands of fur. Matte sculpted smooth animal surface like the frog, very subtle soft material variation. Accessories minimal and removable, not merging with body. Soft neutral studio lighting, broad shapes that read clearly at a small size in a web game.
SPECIES: a small round PANDA traveler, slightly stockier than the frog, proposed standing height 1.15 times the frog. Warm ivory white face and belly, soft charcoal ears, arms and legs, small downturned black eye patches and quiet half-lidded eyes with tiny restrained highlights, short broad muzzle and tiny black nose. Plump pear-shaped belly, two rounded black feet. One small SAGE GREEN triangular neckerchief tied to the side, consistent in all views; a tiny tan canvas tea satchel rests at the left hip on a simple strap, visible appropriately in side and back views. No hat, no bamboo held in its hands, no extra props to occlude body. Character personality: gentle, a little absentminded, would slowly brew bamboo-leaf tea and offer a cup. Keep cute but not babyish, same art direction as the frog.

Half-lidded calm amused eyes and a tiny relaxed mouth. Two short separate legs and rounded cream toe tips; front paws/arms relaxed clear of belly. A moderately thick curved tail curls to one side and is fully shown in profile and back without hiding the legs. Plain muted BLUE triangular neckerchief at neck, no bag on chest and no clothing. A tiny tan rolled sleeping mat attached horizontally across the upper back with simple sage straps, same in all views, a removable accessory. No food held in paws. Personality: proudly lazy, follows warm patches of sunlight, naps on a cushion then stretches. Preserve distinct feline identity, no panda-shaped ears or face. Use the other 3D animal reference only to maintain identical smooth matte sculpting, scale of face details, lighting and presentation.
